techniques.text: Lead with one concrete, source-backed insight that answers a real question for the platform's reader; make the implication clear without inventing outcomes.
Adapt the same evidence separately for Facebook and LinkedIn. Change the hook, explanation and question for each audience instead of copying text across platforms.
Review each assertion for proof. Replace vague superlatives with a verified fact or a narrower, accurate statement.

Name the market topic early using the primary keyword naturally in visible prose. Make the finding understandable without opening the link; never stuff keywords or use hashtags as a substitute for meaning.

Connect one source-backed finding to one concrete business consideration, such as entry, supplier capability or adoption economics. Choose only a consideration the evidence supports; never promise returns or invent a buyer problem.

Use a specific attributed finding instead of hype or a manufactured hot take. Keep the scope and period of a figure. Remove filler, fake personal stories, invented prevailing beliefs and engagement bait.
